html:
Satyajit Ray was a film director from Calcutta, born in 1921, whose Apu Trilogy brought Indian cinema to world attention. He is often named among the greatest directors in the history of film.

He came from a family of writers and artists, studied at Tagore's university at Santiniketan and worked as a designer at an advertising firm. Meeting the French director Jean Renoir in Calcutta and seeing the Italian film Bicycle Thieves in London convinced him to make films about real lives with ordinary actors.

His first film, Pather Panchali of 1955, about a poor village boy named Apu, was made on a tiny budget over several years and won a prize at Cannes. It and its two sequels follow Apu into manhood.

He made about thirty more features, including Charulata and The Music Room, and wrote his own scripts and music. He also wrote popular Bengali stories, among them the detective Feluda. He received an honorary Oscar in 1992, weeks before he died. His calm, humane style influenced directors around the world.
